maria: quick Q — where can I pull p50/p95/p99 for TTFT and tokens/sec for the hosted inference API? trying to correlate a latency spike around the 11:30 deploy. any dashboard/panel names or PromQL snippets I should use?

aj: for TTFT look at the runtime latency dashboard: Grafana -> Redwood / runtime / latency-overview. panels: 'TTFT (first-token latency) by model' and 'Tokens/sec (inflight)'. if you prefer PromQL, try:
```
# TTFT p95 over 5m for model 'redwood-v2'
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(inference_request_first_token_latency_bucket{model="redwood-v2"}[5m])) by (le))

# tokens/sec (moving rate across workers)
sum(rate(runtime_tokens_processed_total[1m])) by (model)
```
also set the Grafana var $model to the service/model you saw in traces.

kevinl: tracing side — use Tempo/Jaeger link from the same dashboard (panel Actions -> Open traces). filter by span name `inference/serve` and tag `model`. sample trace filter in Jaeger UI: `operation=inference/serve and tags.model=redwood-v2 and duration>200ms`. that usually surfaces whether slowdown is in the runtime or downstream (kv cache, db call).

maria: perfect — where do logs live for these requests? want the request_id -> trace_id join.

tara: logs are in Loki. quick Loki query (scope to the runtime pod):
```
{job="runtime",env="prod"} |= "request_id=" | json | request_id=="<id>"
```
we include `trace_id` and `request_id` in structured logs. once you have trace_id you can paste in Jaeger.

aj: for correlation: start with the TTFT p95 bump time window, graph tokens/sec and inflight requests. if tokens/sec drops while inflight rises, it indicates batching stall or model fallback. if tokens/sec steady but TTFT jumps, look at first-span duration in traces (maybe cold-start or quantized path).

kevinl: FYI we recently renamed some metrics — older dashboards use `inference_time_seconds` while new runtime exposes `inference_request_first_token_latency`. if a panel looks off, check the dropdown var `metric_version` or use the `legacy_` prefixed panels. cc @maria if you hit mismatch.

maria: got it. any alert tuning recs? p95 alerts are noisy during rolling deploys.

aj: we tuned p95 alert to 2x baseline and added a 10m cooldown + suppress during rolling deploy tag in deploy-bot. rule is: if p95 > baseline*2 for 3/5m AND not annotated with `deploy_in_progress`, trigger. baseline computed with `predict_linear` on 7d window.

ops-bot: Deploy 1769007200 started by @kevinl (rolling, 6 pods). Flagging channel for suppressed latency alerts. :gear:

maria: ah that explains the noisy window. thanks. last q — any quick query to see p50/p95/p99 on one chart?

tara: yep, combine quantiles in PromQL like this:
```
# returns p50,p95,p99 series for model redwood-v2 over 5m
quantile_over_time(0.50, rate(inference_request_first_token_latency_bucket{model="redwood-v2"}[5m])) or
quantile_over_time(0.95, rate(inference_request_first_token_latency_bucket{model="redwood-v2"}[5m])) or
quantile_over_time(0.99, rate(inference_request_first_token_latency_bucket{model="redwood-v2"}[5m]))
```
(or just add three panels with histogram_quantile(0.50/0.95/0.99, ...)).

kevinl: and to check tokens/sec per worker pod: `rate(runtime_tokens_processed_total{job="runtime"}[1m])` grouped by `pod`. helps spot a single noisy pod.

maria: awesome — this is enough to start. i'll pull the traces and post back findings. thanks y'all :pray: :sparkles:

aj: ping me if you want me to run a manual trace capture or increase sampling for that model for the next hour.
